introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown: An element, **A**, has atomic number 19 and readily reacts with cold water.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Write the electronic configuration of **A**.

(ii) Is **A** a metal or a non-metal? Give a reason for your choice. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Atomic number 19 means 19 protons and 19 electrons, so **A** is potassium (K).

(i) The 19 electrons fill the shells 2, 8, 8, 1: electronic configuration **2, 8, 8, 1**.

(ii) **A is a metal.** Reason: its atom has only **one electron in its outer shell**, which it loses easily to form a positive ion ($\mathrm{K^+}$); it also reacts with water to form an alkaline solution (a metal hydroxide).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Identify the group on the Periodic Table to which the element **A** belongs.

(ii) Give one other element belonging to this group. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Group I** (the alkali metals), because **A** has one outer electron.

(ii) Any one of: **lithium (Li)**, **sodium (Na)**, rubidium (Rb), caesium (Cs).

questions.enonce_markdown: Using electron dot and cross diagrams only, show how the bond between **A** and oxygen is formed. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**A** (potassium) is a metal and oxygen is a non-metal, so the bond is **ionic**: electrons are transferred.

*What to draw (outer shells only):*

1. Two atoms of **A**, each showing one outer electron (drawn as a dot, $\bullet$), and one oxygen atom showing its 6 outer electrons (drawn as crosses, $\times$).
2. An arrow from each potassium atom to the oxygen atom: each potassium atom **transfers its one outer electron** to oxygen.
3. The final diagram: two potassium ions, each shown as $[\mathrm{K}]^+$ (outer shell now empty, charge $+$), and one oxide ion drawn in square brackets with **8 outer electrons** around the symbol O (6 crosses and 2 dots), with the charge $2-$ outside the bracket: $[\mathrm{O}]^{2-}$.

The compound formed is potassium oxide, $\mathrm{K_2O}$: $2\mathrm{K} + \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{O_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{K_2O}$, held together by the electrostatic attraction between $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ions.

questions.enonce_markdown: State one observation when **A** reacts with cold water. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Any one of: the metal **floats and moves about on the surface**, **fizzes (effervescence, hydrogen gas given off)**, melts into a silvery ball, burns with a lilac flame, and finally disappears (dissolves) to give an alkaline solution.

questions.enonce_markdown: Write the formula of the chloride of **A**. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: **A** forms the ion $\mathrm{K^+}$ and chlorine forms $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, so the chloride is **KCl** (potassium chloride).
